nodeData.topic: Law of Business Associations and Insolvency
nodeData.note: How people run businesses together in Kenya, from partnerships to companies under the Companies Act 2015, and what happens when they fail under the Insolvency Act 2015. A draft study aid, not legal advice.

children.note: The legal forms people use to run a business together, and what happens when a business cannot pay its debts.
Sole trader, partnership, limited liability partnership or company. The choice affects who owns, who decides and who pays if it fails.
A mama mboga, a law firm and Safaricom all need a legal form. Picking the right one protects owners and creditors.

manas.q: Name four legal forms a business in Kenya can take.

children.note: Article 36 protects the right to form and join associations, and requires fair process before a registration is cancelled.

manas.q: Which Article of the Constitution protects freedom of association?

children.note: The Partnership Act, Limited Liability Partnerships Act, Companies Act 2015 and Insolvency Act 2015 are the core statutes.

manas.q: Which two 2015 Acts govern Kenyan companies and insolvency?

children.topic: Insolvency is part of the course
children.note: The CLE lists this course as Law of Business Associations, to include Insolvency.
The simplest forms: one person in business, or several in business together.
One person owns and runs the business. No separate legal person exists, so all debts are the owner's personal debts.

manas.q: Is a sole trader's business a separate legal person?

children.note: Two or more people running a business in common to make a profit. It can arise from a written deed, a spoken deal or conduct alone.

manas.q: What are the elements of a partnership?

children.note: Each partner can usually bind the firm in ordinary business dealings, so choose partners carefully.
Partners are personally liable for the firm's debts, so a creditor can reach a partner's own house or car.

manas.q: What is the main risk of an ordinary partnership?

children.note: Unless agreed otherwise, partners share profits equally, all take part in management and are indemnified for proper business costs.
By agreement, expiry, a partner's death, or a court order. Assets go first to pay debts.
Kenya has its own Partnership Act, which follows the English model while also allowing limited partners.
A hybrid under Kenya's Limited Liability Partnerships Act: partners run it like a partnership, but the LLP is a legal person and partners' liability is limited.

manas.q: How does an LLP differ from an ordinary partnership?

children.note: A company is created by registration and becomes a legal person separate from its owners.
Founders file documents with the Registrar of Companies. The certificate of incorporation is the company's birth certificate.
Private or public; limited by shares, limited by guarantee or unlimited. Only public companies can offer shares to the public.
Under the Companies Act 2015, a private company may have a single member, like a one-person matatu business.
The company owns its property, makes contracts, sues and is sued in its own name.
A bootmaker turned his business into a company and held almost all shares. When it failed, the House of Lords held he was not liable for its debts: the company was a separate person.

manas.q: What principle did Salomon v Salomon establish?

children.note: A man owned nearly all shares and was the company's pilot. He could still be its employee, so his widow got compensation.

manas.q: Why could Mr Lee be an employee of his own company?

children.note: A sole shareholder insured timber in his own name, not the company's. His claim failed because the timber belonged to the company.
Shareholders lose only what they put in or promised for their shares. The company's creditors cannot chase their personal assets.

manas.q: What does 'limited liability' mean for a shareholder?

children.note: Rarely, courts look past the company to the people behind it.
The modern English test: the veil may be pierced only where a company is used to dodge a legal duty its controller already had.

manas.q: What is the modern English test for piercing the veil?

children.note: A former employee set up a company to break his promise not to compete. The court stopped him by injunction.
Courts cannot ignore Salomon just because justice seems to demand it; group companies are separate.
The UK Supreme Court narrowed true piercing to evasion of existing obligations. The family homes reached the wife through trust law instead.
Laws on fraudulent or wrongful trading can make directors personally liable when a company fails.
The company's rulebook and how money comes in and out.
The company's internal rules on meetings, directors and shares. Model articles apply where the company has not written its own.

manas.q: What are a company's articles of association?

children.note: The articles bind the company and its members like a contract, so members can enforce some of their rights.
A share is a unit of ownership, giving rights to dividends, votes and a slice of surplus on winding up.
Preference shares usually get dividends first but carry fewer votes. Ordinary shares carry the main risk and control.

manas.q: How do preference shares differ from ordinary shares?

children.note: A company should not hand its capital back to members except as the law allows. Dividends come from profits only.

manas.q: From what may a company pay dividends?

children.note: Companies borrow using debentures and give security. A fixed charge is over a specific asset; a floating charge hovers over changing assets like stock.

manas.q: What is the difference between a fixed and a floating charge?

children.note: Charges must be registered so that later lenders can see what is already pledged. Missing this can make the charge fail against a liquidator.
Who runs the company, who owns it, and how they make decisions.
People who manage the company day to day. A company secretary handles filings and records.
The Companies Act 2015 sets out directors' general duties, drawn from older case law.
Follow the constitution and use powers only for their proper purposes.
Act in good faith for the members as a whole, thinking of employees, suppliers, community and environment.

manas.q: Whose interests must a director promote under the codified duties?

children.note: Act as a reasonably careful director would, judged by the job and by the director's own knowledge.
No using company opportunities for yourself, no bribes from third parties, and declare interests in company deals.
Directors bought shares in a subsidiary and made profits through their office. They had to repay the profit even without fraud or loss to the company.

manas.q: Why did the directors in Regal (Hastings) have to repay their profit?

children.note: Members own the company, but the majority usually rules.
If directors wrong the company, the company itself is the proper claimant, not individual members. The majority may ratify.

manas.q: What is the proper plaintiff rule in Foss v Harbottle?

children.note: Illegal acts, bypassing a special majority, invading a member's personal rights, and fraud on the minority.
Kenya's Companies Act 2015 lets a member, with court permission, sue on the company's behalf for wrongs by directors.
A member whose interests are unfairly harmed by how the company is run can ask the court for a remedy, such as a buy-out.
Members decide key issues by resolution at meetings or in writing.
Passed by a simple majority of votes, for example to appoint a director.

manas.q: What majority does an ordinary resolution need?

children.note: Needs at least 75% of votes, for big decisions like changing the articles or a voluntary winding up.

manas.q: What majority does a special resolution need?

children.note: A regular meeting where members receive accounts and question directors. Rules differ for private and public companies.
What happens when a person or company cannot pay debts. Kenya's Insolvency Act 2015 covers both individuals and companies.
Unable to pay debts as they fall due (cash-flow test) or debts larger than assets (balance-sheet test).

manas.q: What are the two common tests for insolvency?

children.note: A court process for people who cannot pay. A trustee collects and shares out assets, and the person is later discharged.
A debtor and creditors agree a plan to pay part of the debts over time, avoiding bankruptcy or liquidation.
An administrator takes over to rescue the company or get creditors a better result. A moratorium stops creditors suing meanwhile.

manas.q: What is the main aim of administration?

children.note: The end of the road: a liquidator sells assets, pays creditors and the company is dissolved.
Started by members' special resolution. If solvent, members control it; if insolvent, creditors do.
Ordered by the court, usually on a creditor's petition for an unpaid debt.
Roughly: secured creditors, costs, preferential debts like wages, floating charge holders, unsecured creditors, then members last. Kenya's Act sets its own list.

manas.q: Who is paid last in a liquidation?

children.note: Directors who keep trading when they knew or should have known the company could not avoid insolvent liquidation can be made to contribute.

manas.q: When can directors be liable for wrongful trading?

children.note: A public officer who acts in many bankruptcies and liquidations, especially early on or where no private insolvency practitioner is appointed.
Cases above are English or Commonwealth decisions, persuasive in Kenya. Kenyan statutes and courts come first.
Kenya's company and insolvency Acts borrow heavily from English law, so Kenyan courts often cite English cases as persuasive, not binding.
Add the leading Kenyan decisions from Kenya Law (kenyalaw.org).
Kenyan law has its own Acts, registrar and procedures. Always cite the Companies Act 2015 or Insolvency Act 2015 before English authority.
Use IRAC: Issue, Rule, Application, Conclusion.
Achieng owns 99% of Kiambu Feeds Ltd. The company owes a supplier KES 2m and is closing. Can the supplier sue Achieng personally?
Issue: is Achieng liable for the company's debt? Rule: separate personality (Salomon) and limited liability; the veil is lifted only in narrow cases.
Unless Achieng used the company to evade an existing duty, or trading rules apply, the supplier can claim only against the company, likely in liquidation.
Owning almost all shares does not make you the company. Keep person and company apart.

children.topic: Trap: lifting the veil too easily
children.note: Courts rarely pierce the veil. Unfairness alone is not enough.

manas.q: Is unfairness alone enough to lift the corporate veil?

children.note: Once a company nears insolvency, think of creditors and wrongful trading, not just shareholders.
